L153@P10: Dear Armand:
L154@P10: March 16, 1976
L155@P10: Many thanks for your letter of March 1. I have now withdrawn from
L156@P10: the arran,::; ements with :Berkeley and am looking forward to the year at
L157@P10: the Institute.
L158@P10: I am sure that a salary of~ 25.000 will be adequate in spite of
L159@P10: the inflation during the five years since I was last in the US. Of course
L160@P10: I assume then that it will be possible to avoid confrontation with the
L161@P10: Swedish tax problems by beinG' out of Sweden and employed for more than
L162@P10: one year. For this reason I would like the employment at the Institute
L163@P10: to start on September 1 and expect to be there about that time. It should
L164@P10: end at some time well after the end of the academic year. It is yet too
L165@P10: early to make this more precise, for I have to arrange some sort of
L166@P10: employment through September 1978 - with a break for vacation ·which as
L167@P10: far as I know can be taken in Sweden. As yet I have of course made no
L168@P10: plans for this.
L169@P10: I have tried to sum up recent developments related to Fourier
L170@P10: Integral Operators in the pages attached to this letter. Among the
L171@P10: nam·es mentioned it seems to me that the first choice must be Johannes
L172@P10: Sjostrand - although I hesitate to say so since he has been my student.
L173@P10: You can get more infor ation on him from your French connections since
L174@P10: he has spent a couple of years in Nice and Orsay - I think he is maitre
L175@P10: de conference in Orsay. This year he visits Purdue and I have heard
L176@P10: recently that he has been made full professor there although this has
L177@P10: not been confirmed~ (He is quite young, born in 1947.) I have of course
L178@P10: not discussed this matter with him but if you wish I could contact him
L179@P10: informally later on.
L180@P10: My second choice would probably be Boutet de Manvel. However, it
L181@P10: might be useful to wait a while and see how the study of mixed problems
L182@P10: (II.4 in the attached papers) develops.
L183@P10: Sincer~ly yours,

L195@P11: Dear Armand:
L196@P11: Thank you for your letter of January 28. I would be delighted to
L197@P11: spend another year at the Institute, preferably the academic year 77-78.
L198@P11: There is just one problem. In January I was approached by the Berkeley
L199@P11: Mathematics Department and agreed then that they could nominate me for
L200@P11: a Miller Professorship that same year. However, the Mathematics Department has to compete with all science departments so the outcome is not
L201@P11: clear. If the Institute plan can be made final soon, before I hear from
L202@P11: Berkeley, it seems to me that I can still withdraw from the Berkeley
L203@P11: arrangement - and l would prefer to spend the year in Princeton.
L204@P11: In case you decide to have a miniprogram on Fourier Integral Operators
L205@P11: I hope that you give me a chance later on to discuss whom to invite.
L206@P11: However, I should like to comment already now that I do not consider
L207@P11: Duistermaat a first choice at this time. He has not done much for quite
L208@P11: some time now and he had nothing to say when we had a Nordic Summer
L209@P11: School on FIO last summer. On the other hand there are many other ' thi.ngs
L210@P11: going on which one should try to cover.
L211@P11: With best regards,
L212@P11: Sincerely yours,
L213@P11: Lars Hormander

L221@P12: Dear Lars:
L222@P12: January 28, 1976
L223@P12: You may remember that we had sometime special
L224@P12: years at the Institute. It is not anymore financially possible
L225@P12: to organize them. However, we want to try to have smaller
L226@P12: programs. especially to foster activity in important areas
L227@P12: not well represented on the Faculty, notably in analysis.
L228@P12: They would involve one or maybe two senior people and
L229@P12: some younger mathematicians. We would like very much
L230@P12: to have you as the center of one such program, say on
L231@P12: Fourier integral operators, and I am writing to ask
L232@P12: whether you would be interested in spending one of the next
L233@P12: two or three years at the lnstitutt;!. We would then try to
L234@P12: invite for the same period a few people with related interests (e.g. Duistermaat). For this, we would be very
L235@P12: glad to have some suggestions from you. hoping that the
L236@P12: prospect of having a particular mathematician here would
L237@P12: make this invitation more attractive to you.
L238@P12: Sincerely yours,
